title: Cancellation Reasons, Documentation and Refund Methods — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
## C1 — request and status

A cancellation of a policy under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) is processed only on a cancellation request signed by an authorized signer of the named insured and on file for the policy. The policy status must be pending effective or in force when the cancellation is processed, and it is cancelled once processed. Both conditions are read from Tidemark's records — the signed request on file and the policy status.

## C2 — reasons, documents and effective dates

| Reason | Documentation | Cancellation takes effect | Refund method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Building sold | closing disclosure or settlement statement | title transfer date | pro rata |
| Building removed or demolished | evidence of removal | removal date | pro rata |
| Contents sold or removed (contents-only policies) | — | date the contents left the premises | pro rata |
| Duplicate NFIP policy | the other policy's declarations | original effective date of the later-dated policy, which is the one cancelled | full from inception |
| Closing did not occur | lender's statement that the loan did not close | original effective date | full from inception |
| Removed from the Special Flood Hazard Area by a Letter of Map Amendment or Revision | the FEMA Letter of Map Amendment or Revision | current term start | current term full |
| Mortgage paid off | payoff letter | see C3 | pro rata |
| Voluntary — not required | none | see C3 | pro rata |
| Replaced by private flood | the private policy's declarations | see C3 | pro rata |

## C3 — backdating limit

For a mortgage paid off, a voluntary cancellation and a replacement by private flood, the effective date may not be earlier than the tier's voluntary backdating allowance before the date the signed request is received, and for a replacement by private flood it is the private policy's effective date when that is later.

## C4 — lender release

A cancellation for mortgage paid off, voluntary — not required, replaced by private flood, or removed from the Special Flood Hazard Area on a mortgage-required policy needs the lender's written release on file.

## C5 — refund methods

The refund method follows the reason: full from inception returns every component booked on the policy, fees included; current term full returns the current term's risk premium, ICC premium, Reserve Fund Assessment and HFIAA surcharge in full; pro rata returns the same four components of the current term multiplied by the days from the cancellation effective date to the term end divided by the days from the term start to the term end. *This clause is no longer in force for the cancellation credits of a policy whose current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit; where those terms carry more, it remains in force as written.*

## C6 — rounding and fees

Each component is rounded half-up to the tier's refund rounding increment before the components are added. Under current term full and pro rata the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge are fully earned. *That sentence on fees is no longer in force for a cancellation refund whose current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit, each counted by its risk premium entries; for a cancellation refund whose terms carry more than one premium-bearing endorsement or more than one re-rate credit, and for every other Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge, it stands.*

## C7 — claim bar

No refund at all is due for the current term under the reasons mortgage paid off, voluntary — not required, replaced by private flood, and removed from the Special Flood Hazard Area, when a claim with a date of loss in the current term has been paid (a claim whose payments net of voids are above zero) or is still open (a reported claim with neither a payment nor a denial on record); the cancellation still proceeds. *This clause is no longer in force as written for the cancellation credits of the risk premium, the ICC premium, the Reserve Fund Assessment and the HFIAA surcharge; in every other case the claim bar stands as written.*

## C8 — booking and notice

Each refunded component is booked as a cancellation credit referencing the cancellation request, and the total is refunded to the payor of record. *This clause is no longer in force for a cancellation refund as to when its credits are booked, and, for a cancellation refund whose current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit, each counted by its risk premium entries, as to what the refund adds; a cancellation refund whose terms carry more than one premium-bearing endorsement or more than one re-rate credit is the total of its credits alone, and every other refund remains the total of the credits it settles.* When the policy is mortgage-required, the mortgagee of record is notified of the cancellation.

The components a current-term-full or pro rata refund can return are the risk premium, ICC premium, Reserve Fund Assessment and HFIAA surcharge. *Scoped exception:* for a cancellation refund whose current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit, each counted by its risk premium entries, the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge of a term that began after the cancellation took effect are returned in full as well, while those of the term in which a cancellation under current term full or pro rata takes effect stay fully earned, and the refund also adds the premium received but not owed.
